memory_update.text: WEST should remain a primary underfollowed candidate for the private-label coffee, extracts and beverage solutions node because its filings directly map to sourcing, traceability, roasting, packaging, extracts, RTD, foodservice and restaurant customers.

FARM is a high-relevance but financially speculative micro-cap exception; later layers must prioritize balance sheet, cash generation, customer retention and DSD route economics before it can survive the funnel.
THS is a second-order underfollowed private-label coffee manufacturing candidate because its coffee capabilities may be buried inside a broader private-label packaged-food profile.

Several important private-label coffee and extract suppliers appear private or not US-listed, including Finlays, Bunn-O-Matic, Gaviña and other niche extract/co-manufacturing players; later passes should decide whether public beneficiaries are mainly asset-light suppliers, distributors, or branded platforms rather than pure-play extract makers.

WEST is the clearest direct public candidate for the private-label coffee, tea, extract, traceability, and foodservice beverage-solutions node, but should be treated as high-risk until debt, cash flow, utilization, and customer concentration are verified.

FARM is a highly underfollowed micro-cap direct foodservice coffee and beverage-service candidate; relevance is strong but financial durability and post-asset-sale business scope must be verified before advancing.

THS is a second-order private-label platform candidate because it acquired Farmer Brothers coffee-related assets, but coffee/foodservice materiality may be diluted inside a broader private-label food portfolio.

Need primary filings for all candidates, especially customer concentration, restaurant/foodservice revenue mix, private-label contract duration, extract capacity, roasting capacity, capex needs, and gross-margin sensitivity to green coffee prices.

Restaurant chains increasingly centralize procurement or internalize distribution, but beverage-menu expansion can still create outsourced bottlenecks in sourcing, roasting, extraction, traceability, and DSD/service infrastructure.

WEST is the cleanest underfollowed public-market mapping for private-label coffee, extracts, RTD, beverage development, and restaurant/foodservice beverage solutions; prioritize for Layer 2 evidence review.

THS is a useful reference/small-cap context name after acquiring Farmer Brothers' Northlake coffee facility; verify how much coffee exposure is material inside the broader private-label packaged-food portfolio.
FARM is highly node-relevant through DSD, foodservice coffee, equipment service, and restaurant/customer coverage, but market cap and likely financial fragility require speculative-shadow treatment.
JVA is a micro-cap discovery lead for private-label and wholesale coffee; restaurant exposure is plausible but weaker and must be verified through channel/customer disclosures.

The node appears investable through B2B coffee/beverage platforms, private-label manufacturing, direct-store-delivery service networks, coffee equipment/service vendors, and extract/RTD capabilities rather than only through branded coffee chains.

Need later-layer search for non-obvious public vendors in beverage formulation, aseptic/RTD co-packing, flavor/extract ingredients, restaurant coffee equipment/service, foodservice distributors' private-label coffee programs, and quality/testing/certification gates.

WEST is the cleanest public-market mapping for the private-label coffee, extracts, traceability, and beverage-solutions node, but later layers must test leverage, capex intensity, extract-facility utilization, customer concentration, and sustainable margins.

FARM and JVA have unusually direct coffee/foodservice/private-label exposure but are below the preferred market-cap range; keep them only as speculative shadow candidates until filings prove liquidity, profitability, and customer durability.

THS is a broader private-label manufacturer with possible beverage and coffee optionality; the next layer should determine whether coffee/tea/private-label beverage is material or merely a small tuck-in exposure.

The restaurant beverage supply-chain node appears to split into four public-market subnodes: integrated beverage solutions and extracts, DSD foodservice coffee distribution, private-label packaged beverage manufacturing, and niche wholesale roasting/green-coffee sourcing.

Commercial coffee equipment and service may be a real chokepoint, but BUNN is private after Ali Group's 2026 acquisition and many equipment specialists are private or embedded inside diversified foodservice equipment companies; later passes should search public equipment/service proxies separately.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found a concentrated public universe for B2B coffee, private-label beverage, extract, and foodservice beverage solutions. The strongest direct underfollowed exposures are Westrock Coffee, TreeHouse Foods, and Farmer Bros.; Keurig Dr Pepper is included as a high-attention reference anchor because its coffee systems, pods, away-from-home channels, and planned coffee separation help benchmark the node but it is less aligned with the underfollowed discovery lane. Layer 1B expansion for the restaurant beverage-supply node finds a small universe of US-listed suppliers where the economic exposure can sit behind restaurant, hospitality, convenience-store, and private-label beverage menus. The cleanest direct fits are Westrock Coffee and Farmer Brothers; TreeHouse Foods is a second-order private-label platform with specific coffee assets acquired from Farmer Brothers; Coffee Holding is a micro-cap speculative shadow candidate that may be relevant but needs primary-source verification before advancing. Evidence quality is uneven, so later layers should prioritize 10-K segment disclosure, customer concentration, debt/cash-flow durability, foodservice exposure, and whether scaled roasting/extract capacity is actually constrained.
